name: Refined Listings
description: Virtual staging and marketing toolkit for real estate agents and property managers: MLS import, multi-angle staging, a style catalog, object removal, and photo-to-video (company-stated). The founder says they did $800k+ lifetime as an agency, then moved to software in Oct 2025. Pricing is pay-as-you-go credit packs from $128 to $750, with about an 18% repeat purchase rate (company-stated). ~3,500 users (founder-stated). Listed for sale at $495,000, about 1.4× (TrustMRR).

mentions.evidence: ~$29,357 L30 (−23.5%), ~$94,669 last 3 months, ~$149,539 last 6 months, ~$232,667 last 12 months, ~$266,829 all-time. MRR snapshot ~$752, 8 active subscriptions. Credit packs dominate over a classic monthly seat figure. L30 profit margin 68% (TrustMRR snapshot). Asking price $495,000. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~07:17 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: Credits, not seats, for one realtor workflow (staging, floor plans, listing video). Sell packs.

whyItPrints: Agents need listing photos that sell. Credits beat seats when usage is bursty. A clear buyer and a sale listing.
whyThisMatters:
Listing photos sell houses, and an empty room sells worse than a furnished one. Refined Listings stages the photo. An agent uploads images or imports a listing, tries styles, removes objects, and restages the same room from more than one angle. Staging itself is free. A credit is spent when the full-resolution file is downloaded for the MLS. Credits do not expire, and unused ones can be refunded for a week. The site also sells a short listing film, a walkthrough made from stills, and a one-listing website.

The live packs are one-time downloads, not a monthly seat. That matches the Stripe record, where a handful of subscriptions sit far below cash in the last 30 days. The founder says the business was an agency first, with a large lifetime total, and became software in late 2025. The founder-stated user count is a few thousand. The listing is for sale at a price a bit above the last year of Stripe cash. Teams and brokerages can get volume pricing and a co-branded login.

You pay when a staged photo is good enough to put on the listing, not on the first day of the month.
